description: A batched extract with no trailer -- a header, then details until the next header -- whose two discriminators sit at different offsets and different widths: the header's three bytes at the front, the detail's one byte behind a ten-byte account number. The two runs share no byte, so no literal either record could carry separates them, and what reads the file is the order the state carries: the header's test is tried first because its run begins at the earlier byte, and a record that fails it is read as a detail. The items covering each run inside the opposing record are both PIC X, so the copybooks prove nothing in either direction and the pair rests on the order alone -- which is what the layout asserts about its data by being written this way, and what batch-disjoint is the other outcome of. The fourth record is where the order decides: it is a second header, reached at a state where both records are eligible.
source: docs/layout/SPEC.md, "A batch boundary, told by the order", whose copybooks these are; docs/ir/SPEC.md, "A batch boundary is told by the order", "Transitions are ordered by what they read" and "When two match, and when none does"
